claims.text: What AFFTC Detachment 3 is, per Peter W. Merlin's own published reference work on Groom Lake: 'Since the late 1970s, the Groom Lake facility has been operated by Detachment 3 of the Air Force Flight Test Center (DET 3 AFFTC) under Air Force Systems Command (AFSC) and later Air Force Materiel Command (AFMC).' The identification is Tier 2 because it rests on a named historian's published site and not on any primary Air Force unit history opened here.

claims.text: On what Detachment 3 of the Air Force Flight Test Center is, in his own published reference work: 'Since the late 1970s, the Groom Lake facility has been operated by Detachment 3 of the Air Force Flight Test Center (DET 3 AFFTC) under Air Force Systems Command (AFSC) and later Air Force Materiel Command (AFMC).' This is the statement that gives Fouche's AF Form 77a of 24 August 1979 its meaning.

a.label: AF Form 77a, Letter of Evaluation, 24 August 1979

edges.label: Records temporary duty to AFFTC Detachment 3, the unit operating Groom Lake, 1 June to 14 August 1979
edges.note: TIER 2 IS THE CEILING AND HERE IS WHY. The form itself says 'AFFTC-DET 3, Nellis AF Range', which is Tier 1. The identification of DET 3 AFFTC with Groom Lake rests on Peter Merlin's own published site and not on any primary Air Force unit history, organisational chart or FOIA release opened by this research. The weaker link sets the tier.

b.label: AF Form 77a, Letter of Evaluation, 24 August 1979

edges.label: His own published work is what establishes what AFFTC Detachment 3 is
edges.note: THIS EDGE IS THE INVERSE OF THE TWO ABOVE AND IS BUILT SEPARATELY ON PURPOSE. The same historian whose analysis demolishes most of Fouche's account is the reference source that makes Fouche's single best document mean something: 'Since the late 1970s, the Groom Lake facility has been operated by Detachment 3 of the Air Force Flight Test Center.' He is on both sides of this file and the graph should show it.
